sections.h2: What the Register of Deeds records in Lumberton
sections.html:
Anything that transfers or encumbers land in Robeson County ends up here: the deed to your buyer, the buyer's deed of trust, the cancellation of your old loan, plats and similar papers. Call 910-671-3040 with questions about a recording.

State statute bars the office from giving legal advice or preparing deeds, and it keeps no forms. Its recording page tells filers to see an attorney for any legal question and for drafting.

Recording matters because of G.S. 47-18, which works like a queue. A deed protects its holder against outside claims from the moment it is registered locally, and earlier registration wins.

Every deed needs tax certification before recording, unless it comes with the delinquent tax statement under G.S. 161-31. A deed mailed without either one is returned to the sender.

The certification comes from the county tax department, not the register. That makes the tax office the first stop for a Robeson deed, and it is the step sellers most often forget.

Ways to get a Robeson County deed certified by the tax office
MethodHow to do it
EmailSend the documents to deeds@robesoncountync.gov
MailRobeson County Tax Department, 550 North Chestnut Street, 2nd Floor, Lumberton NC 28358
PhoneCall the tax office at 910-671-3060 for instructions

Ask your closing attorney whether the firm already requests certification for every deed it sends. Many firms do, but a seller handling a family transfer or a sale without an attorney has to do it personally.

Every document recorded in person must show a return name and mailing address. If you bring no stamped, self-addressed envelope, a $1.00 mailing fee is added.

The paper must be drafted, signed and notarized before it arrives. Staff can't repair a bad acknowledgment or write in missing terms. If the notary left out a seal or a date, the document has to go back to be fixed before you return. Bring this:

  • Tax certification or the delinquent tax statement attached.
  • A return name and address on the document.
  • An envelope addressed to you with postage, or a dollar for the office to mail it.
  • The signed, notarized original.

Mailed packages follow the same rules, so include the certification from the start. A call to 910-671-3040 can settle questions about a specific filing, and the county also hosts online deed search tools through its records page.

These are statewide figures from G.S. 161-10, the same across North Carolina. Fifteen pages of an ordinary instrument cost $26, and each added page is $4. Loan documents get 35 pages for $64. Recording a loan cancellation is free.

Plats cost $21 per sheet. A certified copy starts at $5, with $2 for each added page. A document in nonstandard form adds $25, and each extra instrument in the same packet adds $10. Fees are paid before filing, so budget for them at closing, along with the mailing fee if it applies.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed excise tax?
sections.html:
The seller pays it, under G.S. 105-228.30. The transferor pays the register before filing, at a dollar for each $500 of value, with any fraction counted as a whole $500.

Half stays with Robeson County. The rest goes to the state revenue department every month after refunds, and the county may keep 2 percent of that state half. A parcel split between counties is taxed where more of its value sits.

Your closing attorney should print the amount on your settlement statement. If you want a figure early, give the register's staff the sale price.

Whoever owns the parcel on January 1 owes for the year, and a later sale does not clear the seller's liability. Proration is a private agreement between buyer and seller, and the seller is mailed the bill for the year of transfer.

To be safe, ask for payment to the tax collector at closing. If the new bill isn't due yet, the collector takes a prepayment based on the previous year's rate. A past-due bill on a property that sold during the year can result in both names being advertised.

The tax office that issues the certification is the same one to ask about your balance, so a single call can cover both.

The tax administrator's Land Records and Mapping section assigns each tract a parcel identification number. Other county departments use it for owner, acreage, value and zoning. The GIS and Addressing section sits in the same division. Quote the parcel number when you contact the tax office about certification, so staff can pull the right record.

The tax office also accepts online and phone payments. The phone line is 1-866-249-0705, and a convenience fee applies.

  • Parcel number: ask the mapping section or find it on your tax bill.
  • Real property: listed permanently, so no annual listing is needed.
  • Bills: mailed in August and due September 1.

Before closing, make sure the tax figure the buyer's attorney requests matches what the collector tells you. Keep the payment confirmation with your closing file, along with the certification the tax office gave for the deed.

sections.h2: Other filings that can accompany a sale
sections.html:
A satisfaction clears your mortgage, and the office charges nothing to record it. Under G.S. 47-18, options, contracts to convey, leases past three years and rights of first refusal bind later buyers only when registered. Under Chapter 47H, an owner-financed contract for deed or a memorandum of it must be recorded within five business days.

  • Check that your payoff results in a recorded satisfaction.
  • Keep copies of every recorded paper.
  • Ask whether a plat or easement affects the lot.

A closing attorney can list every document headed to the register before the day arrives. If you're selling without one, write your own list and check each item off as it is recorded.

Contact the tax office for certification as soon as the deed is drafted, not on closing day. The certification has to be in hand before the register will accept the paper. Confirm that the deed carries a return address and that an envelope or postage is ready.

After filing, follow up with the register to confirm the book and page, and ask the title company or attorney for a copy of the recorded deed. Keep the receipt for fees and the excise tax with your closing papers. If anything comes back to you, read the reason first. The usual causes are missing tax certification or a missing return address.

faqs.q: Can Robeson County register of deeds staff advise me on a deed?
faqs.a: No. State statute bars the office from giving legal advice or preparing deeds, and it has no forms. Take drafting questions to an attorney before the signing.

faqs.q: What if a deed is mailed to Robeson County without certification?
faqs.a: The office returns it to the sender. Every deed needs tax certification or the delinquent tax statement before it can be recorded.

faqs.q: How do I get tax certification for a Robeson deed?
faqs.a: Email deeds@robesoncountync.gov, mail the document to the Tax Department at 550 North Chestnut Street, 2nd Floor, Lumberton, or phone 910-671-3060 for instructions.

faqs.q: Does Robeson County charge for mailing back a recorded deed?
faqs.a: Yes, $1.00, when you record in person and bring no addressed, stamped return envelope. The document must also carry a return name and mailing address.

faqs.q: Does the seller or the buyer owe the excise tax in Robeson County?
faqs.a: The seller does. The tax is $1.00 per $500 of value and is paid to the register before the deed is recorded.
